title: CSS specificity, the short version
description: The rules I actually use, without the formal specificity-scoring explanation.
body:
Inline styles beat everything. After that, count selectors: IDs beat classes, classes beat elements. When two rules tie exactly, the one written later in the file wins.

What actually trips people up

  • A tag selector like div is weaker than a class, even one that appears first in the file.
  • !important should be treated as a last resort, not a tool.
  • Nested selectors stack specificity, so a deeply nested rule can quietly out-rank a simpler one you wrote later.

When in doubt, keep selectors flat and specific to a single class rather than chaining parent selectors.

title: Second law of thermodynamics, plain language
description: Study notes from second-year physics, kept because they finally made entropy click.
body:
Heat moves from hot to cold on its own, never the other way around, unless something else does work to force it.

Entropy is a way of counting how many ways the small stuff inside a system could be arranged and still look the same from the outside. Isolated systems trend toward the arrangement with the most possible configurations, because that arrangement is simply the most likely one.

Why this mattered for the exam

Every question came back to one thing: work with total entropy of system plus surroundings, not just the system alone.

title: Papyrus scripting gotchas
description: Things that cost me hours while building the weather mod, written down so future me doesn't repeat them.
body:
Papyrus compiles silently succeed even when a script reference is null at runtime — check the log, not the compiler.

  • OnUpdate events drift if the game is paused mid-timer.
  • Weather scripts run on their own thread; don't assume ordering against quest scripts.
  • Always test in a fresh save, not your main save, once state gets weird it stays weird.
